settings.heading: Good questions.
settings.text: Everything you want to know about HYPR, your order and your subscription.

settings.question: What is HYPR?
settings.answer: One watermelon scoop with electrolytes, 5 g creatine and 5 g collagen. It replaces three separate tubs with one.

settings.question: Who is it for?
settings.answer: Athletes, sports families and anyone with an active routine. You don’t need to be a pro. Electrolyte needs depend on how much you sweat, eat and drink.

settings.question: How do I use it?
settings.answer: Mix one scoop with 16–24 oz of cold water once a day, rest days too. Follow the label on your tub.

settings.question: Is there sugar or anything artificial?
settings.answer: No sugar. No artificial flavors or dyes. HYPR is sweetened with stevia and colored with beet root.

settings.question: Does combining them work better than taking them apart?
settings.answer: No study shows that. The win is simple: one tub, one scoop, one habit that’s easier to keep.

settings.question: Is collagen the same as protein powder?
settings.answer: No. Collagen isn’t a complete protein. HYPR adds to your routine. It doesn’t replace meals or your protein.

settings.question: Is creatine safe for teens?
settings.answer: Creatine is one of the most studied sports supplements. A 2026 guide for pediatricians says 3–5 g a day can be reasonable for teens who train hard and eat enough. Talk with your doctor first. HYPR is labeled for [AGE GUIDANCE FROM LABEL].

settings.question: When should I take it?
settings.answer: Any time that’s easy to remember. Creatine works by building up, so every day matters more than timing.

settings.question: Do I need electrolytes every day?
settings.answer: Not always. For short, easy workouts, water and food may be enough. They matter most when it’s hot, sessions run long or you sweat a lot.

settings.question: How does subscribe & save work?

settings.question: Who gets the free bottle?
